messages.recipient_title: Vice President Political and Public Affairs
messages.subject: For Stein Hernes | Political & Public Affairs | Executive Value Proposal
messages.body:
Dear Mr. Hernes,

I am writing from Guyana, where I serve as Liaison Director, Social Responsibility at AGM Inc., part of Zijin Mining Group. My mandate spans government and regulatory relations, ESG, corporate affairs, stakeholder strategy and executive coordination across a major industrial operation.

Your Political and Public Affairs remit is directly relevant to the work I have built at the operating interface. I manage institutional relationships across mining, environment, energy, labour, aviation, standards, taxation, trade and investment, while translating external requirements into internal ownership, evidence and executive decisions. I also support stakeholder governance around a 46-50 MWp solar platform and more than 80 MWh of battery storage.

Rather than sending a conventional CV alone, I prepared an Equinor-specific Strategic Value Creation Proposal. It focuses on political and public affairs, government stakeholder architecture, transition credibility and international country-facing execution. My three-page Executive CV forms the final section.

My proposition is not to present myself as a Norwegian policy specialist. It is to bring proven international institutional leadership from another high-scrutiny resource sector and apply it where Equinor needs stronger coordination across governments, sustainability, operations and executive decision-making. I am open to relocation and employer-supported work authorization.

I would value a short confidential conversation about current or emerging Director, Head or senior leadership needs where this combination would add value.

Kind regards,
Ragunauth Ramsaroop
Liaison Director, Social Responsibility
AGM Inc. | Zijin Mining Group
ragunauthramsaroop@icloud.com
ragunauthramsaroop.com

strategic_brief.title: Strategic Value Creation Proposal: Political & Public Affairs, Energy Transition and International Stakeholder Leadership
strategic_brief.prepared_for_title: Vice President Political and Public Affairs
strategic_brief.executive_summary: Equinor operates at the intersection of energy security, decarbonisation, national policy, major capital investment and public legitimacy. My contribution would be to strengthen the translation layer between external institutions and internal execution. I bring director-level experience coordinating ministries, regulators, operating teams and executives in a high-scrutiny multinational environment, combined with practical exposure to renewable-energy deployment, ESG governance, carbon-data accountability and country-facing stakeholder strategy. The strongest fit is a political and public affairs, government relations, sustainability or international stakeholder mandate where disciplined institutional engagement must lead to clear executive decisions and measurable follow-through.
strategic_brief.company_context: Equinor is balancing secure energy supply with a long-term transition strategy across oil and gas, power, renewables and lower-carbon solutions. That operating model places political and public affairs close to value creation because permitting, industrial policy, public acceptance, energy-market design, local value creation and institutional trust can materially affect project timing, investment choices and reputation. Equinor also recruits experienced professionals globally and maintains a dedicated People and Organisation function. The leadership challenge is not only to understand policy. It is to connect external signals to business priorities, align internal owners, engage governments credibly and ensure commitments made to public institutions are converted into operating actions with evidence and accountability.

opportunities.title: Political intelligence to executive choices
opportunities.rationale: Energy policy becomes commercially relevant when leadership can see the implications for projects, market position, investment timing, reputation and institutional relationships. Large organisations lose speed when external developments are distributed across functions without a single decision-oriented view.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would convert policy and government signals into concise executive briefs with implications, options, accountable owners, engagement priorities and escalation points, using the same approach I apply across multiple public-agency interfaces today.

opportunities.title: Government stakeholder architecture
opportunities.rationale: Major energy projects depend on structured relationships with ministries, regulators, local authorities, industry bodies and strategic partners. Influence is strongest when engagement objectives, decision-makers, messages and follow-up obligations are mapped before issues become urgent.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would build tiered stakeholder maps and issue plans that connect senior relationships to specific business outcomes, document commitments and create a recurring rhythm for executive review and follow-through.

opportunities.title: Transition credibility and public legitimacy
opportunities.rationale: Energy-transition strategy is judged through evidence of execution, local value, environmental performance and consistency between public commitments and operating reality. Weak linkage between sustainability narratives and physical operating evidence creates avoidable trust and assurance risk.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would link sustainability claims to operating evidence, stakeholder expectations and project decisions, drawing on renewable-energy governance and carbon-data work in a mining environment where external scrutiny and evidence quality are material.

opportunities.title: International country-facing execution
opportunities.rationale: Equinor's international footprint creates recurring situations where legal, commercial, sustainability, communications and country teams must move together. Many delays arise from fragmented ownership rather than lack of technical expertise.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would establish practical issue-management structures with owners, deadlines, decision gates and documented closure, strengthening execution where government relations, ESG, reputation and operations intersect.

days_0_30: Map priority political and regulatory files, institutions, internal owners and current engagement channels.
Identify where external intelligence loses executive or commercial relevance.
days_31_60: Introduce a concise government-relations decision brief and stakeholder action tracker.
Build engagement plans for priority authorities and industry institutions.
days_61_90: Advance two high-value institutional workstreams to measurable next steps.
Create scenario notes linking policy outcomes to project, market and reputation implications.
days_91_180: Embed the operating rhythm across selected country and corporate interfaces.
Use live files to refine governance, escalation and evidence standards.

potential_impact: Faster conversion of public-policy developments into executive decisions and accountable action.
Stronger institutional relationships linked to clear business objectives.
Lower execution risk where government relations, sustainability and project delivery intersect.
Improved evidence and follow-through behind external commitments.
background_relevance: Director-level responsibility spanning government and regulatory relations, ESG, social responsibility, corporate affairs, stakeholder strategy and executive coordination within a multinational mining operation.

Senior engagement across institutions responsible for mining, environment, energy, labour, aviation, standards, taxation, trade and investment, with documented follow-through across operating functions.

Stakeholder-governance exposure around approximately 46-50 MWp of solar capacity and more than 80 MWh of battery storage, plus a carbon-data pilot built from a 52.6 million-litre fuel baseline, 34 entities, 408 monthly entries and 592 equipment IDs.
Experience aligning Environment, HSE, Legal, Finance, Operations, Procurement, HR, Security, Aviation and technical teams around external commitments, evidence and executive decisions.
